text.intro:
Which measurement carries the Addis offset: an answer to the question the 9 Nov status page left open, from data already in
the repository (233 Addis filters of the 7 Nov closeout). A results page, not a recorded meeting. Exploratory: no Addis
filter has thermal (TOR) EC, so the absolute level stays a range. Written account: docs/addis-reference-closure-2026-11-10.md.
text.linearity:
**HIPS bends; FTIR EC does not.** Against HIPS optical BC the published FTIR EC reads
2.31x − 6.17 µg/m³. Two instruments cannot say which one is not
proportional, so this uses a third as the instrument: the exponent b in Y ∝ X^b, free of the flattening that noise in X causes
in a log-log fit. Against the aethalometer, **HIPS rises to the power 0.51** (0.47–0.56; instrument PM2.5 mass) or
0.49 (potassium), while **FTIR EC rises to the power 1.13** (1.05–1.23) or 1.22. PM2.5 mass is gravimetric
and potassium is XRF: neither is optical or FTIR, so this does not rest on trusting one optical instrument over another.
233 Addis filters; 172 with an aethalometer match, 188 with PM2.5 mass, 189 with a published EC.
text.response:
**Linearising HIPS with a constant fitted elsewhere removes the offset.** The saturation ceiling fitted on Beijing,
Pasadena and Delhi with Addis held out (3 Nov) is 2.07 (1.75–2.49); Addis optical depth has a median of
0.96 and reaches 1.51. Applying that ceiling, the published fit moves from
2.31x − 6.17 to **0.44x + 0.58**
(intercept +1.96 to -0.55 across the ceiling's interval), and linearised HIPS
becomes proportional to the aethalometer (power 1.02). The correction is large
(median × 1.87) and multiplies noise on the heaviest filters. The remaining slope is the
level question: FTIR EC would need a MAC near 21 m²/g to agree.
text.errors: **FTIR EC is about as precise as the aethalometer at Addis.** FTIR EC, SPARTAN published 16 % (9–23); Aethalometer IR BCc 13 % (8–19); HIPS Fabs 21 % (17–24). Random error from three-way agreement alone (log-space triple collocation), on a common scale. It says how tightly each follows the shared day-to-day signal, not how accurate its level is.
text.season:
**Within lot 251 the published FTIR EC has no season effect against the aethalometer:** median FTIR ÷ aethalometer is
0.66 in Bega, 0.66 in Belg and 0.67 in Kiremt. The low Bega value seen before comes from the
18 lot-248 filters of December 2022 to early 2023 (0.53), a lot or early-record question rather
than seasonal chemistry. HIPS / 10 over the same rows falls from 0.85 to
0.54: Kiremt has the highest concentrations, so compressed HIPS reads lowest there.
text.level:
**What is left for FTIR is one level factor, and the existing data bracket it at about × 1.0 to 1.5.** On held-out
IMPROVE sites the calibration reads thermal EC lower the lower the OC/EC: median FTIR ÷ TOR is 0.99 above OC/EC 4
and 0.64 below 1.5 (n 10). Addis FTIR OC/EC has a median of 1.34. The aethalometer scaled by
Pasadena or Delhi, linearised HIPS at the Adama MAC, and PM2.5 mass closure point the same way. Mass closure also caps it: published EC
reconstructs 89 % of gravimetric PM2.5, × 1.5 reaches 100 % and × 1.9 gives 108 %, so
the aethalometer or linearised HIPS read at MAC 10 cannot be EC. None of this is thermal EC measured at Addis.
text.network:
**Addis is the heaviest SPARTAN site optically, and the most compressed.** With PM2.5 mass as the instrument no
aethalometer is needed, so the same exponent can be read at every site. Addis has the highest median optical depth
(0.95) and the lowest exponent of HIPS against FTIR EC (0.46); Dhaka is next on
both (0.73; 0.69). A first pass: sites where the interval is wider than 0.6 are
left off the chart (11 of 23), and the two Chilean sites need a second look before anyone quotes them.
text.next:
**Proposed position.** Carry the published FTIR EC forward with no intercept or seasonal correction and a stated level range.
Stop using Fabs / 10 as the Addis yardstick without linearising. The proposed TOR pass band (0.8 to 1.25) sits where the existing
evidence predicts the answer (about 0.67 to 1.0), so ten filters would most likely read "inconclusive": decide before they arrive
whether the deliverable is pass or fail, or an estimated level factor, and ask for HIPS on the same filters with a few loaded to
Addis optical depth. Optical agreement is still not thermal EC.
